clue.text: Criminal file that's wrong put right

indicators.note: the word file is said to be wrong, so its letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A clerk fixes a mistaken entry in a criminal's records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wrong' rearranges FILE into LIFE, and 'put' joins on R for right. 'Criminal' looks like an adjective for the file but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, so slang for a convict.

clue.text: No salt!

parts.note: salt is slang for a sailor, so this means someone who is no seaman, a person happier ashore

explanation.definitionFit: A landlubber is a person unused to the sea, the opposite of an old sailor.

clue.text: Used to speak highly of latest fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of of latest are formed anew

explanation.surface: Someone praises the newest trend in clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is a verb here, shaping OF LATEST into the answer. 'speak highly' looks like praise but means using a high voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is the artificially high voice a man uses above his normal range.

clue.text: Held in remand perhaps, so paid for release

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of remand and so might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A prisoner held on remand is freed after money changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges REMAND SO; 'Held in' sets the scene of captivity, joining fodder and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive is ransomed when money is handed over to buy their freedom.

clue.text: Individually produced, the servant said

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of the servant word, not its spelling

parts.note: a handmaid is an old word for a female servant

explanation.surface: A maid explains that the goods were made one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: HANDMAID, an old word for a female servant, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods crafted one at a time by a worker rather than by machine are made by hand.

clue.text: The lady's ring is one much admired

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman, the lady's
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A woman's engagement ring is greatly admired.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a person idolised for courage or achievement.

clue.text: Corrupt passage

explanation.surface: A tainted route through the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to pollute or make impure, and a defile is a narrow gorge troops march through in single file.

clue.text: A jolly girl for the fleet

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman is chosen to represent the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective for the girl but is slang for a Royal Marine, RM; 'for the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large force of warships, as in the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Current rise is correct

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word goes upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: A claim that the present upturn is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns TIDE upwards in this down entry; 'is' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it, putting errors right.

clue.text: Not one who yearns — not any more

parts.note: no as a short word of refusal stands for not
to long is to yearn, so a person who yearns is a longer

explanation.surface: Someone says they have stopped yearning, with no wish left at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'longer' not as the comparative of long but as someone who longs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a former state has ended, a straight synonym for formerly but not now.

clue.text: After an order, is the worker showing respect?

indicators.note: after says the remaining words follow the order in the answer

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
taken as written
the ant is the crossword's usual worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an employee given a command is being suitably deferential.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire; a worker ant gives ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant describes someone bowing or deferring, an attitude of reverence.

clue.text: Freshly minted trade-mark three-quarters finished

indicators.note: finished says the three-quarters piece comes at the finish, ending the answer

parts.note: a brand is a trade mark or name
the quarters are the four compass points N, E, S, W; three of them give N, E, W

explanation.surface: A new trademark is said to be three-quarters complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are called quarters in crosswords, so three of them give NEW; 'finished' puts them at the end of BRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand new is fresh from the maker, like a coin just struck at the mint.

clue.text: Admit having originally told untruths, made to retire

indicators.note: originally says the told-untruths piece comes first, at the start of the answer

parts.note: to tell untruths is to lie, so in the past tense lied
to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: A liar is forced to confess and then step down from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' looks like quitting a job but here means going to bed; 'made to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to bed for rest, which is to recline.

clue.text: Mention a different name

indicators.note: different asks for the words mention a in a different letter order

explanation.surface: Someone cites an alternative name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges MENTION A. 'Mention' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'name', a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate is to put someone forward for a post, to propose them by naming.

clue.text: Usually one should admit a grave wrong

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the one word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wrong signals the words a grave are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Advice that a person ought to confess to a serious error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as serious, but its letters are anagram fodder with 'a'; 'wrong' signals the shuffle and 'should admit' the insertion between N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that holds as a rule in most cases happens typically, the normal run of things.

clue.text: Sailors on a course — of medicine?

indicators.note: on here means the sailors are placed at the course, the two words joined course first

parts.note: Epsom is a racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby
salts is slang for sailors, old seamen

explanation.surface: Seamen at the races wonder about medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is an English racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run; 'of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are magnesium sulphate crystals taken as a laxative or used in a bath.

clue.text: Wayward son demands bride's tolerance

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the path, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A rebellious son's demands put his bride's patience to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wayward' rearranges all the letters of SON DEMANDS BRIDE; the possessive adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-minded and accepting of others' views is a form of patience with difference.

clue.text: Liberation, in a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Freedom, and how a speaker sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery can mean rescue or setting free, and also the way a speech is spoken aloud.

clue.text: More of the same in Latin

definitions.text: More of the same in Latin

parts.words: More of the same in Latin
parts.note: the Latin phrase meaning and the rest, used to cut a list short

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase signals that a list continues with similar items, abbreviated etc.

clue.text: Limit the drink, it makes good sense

parts.note: to ration something is to limit how much can be had
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Cutting back on alcohol is advised as the sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it makes' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind a choice, the logic that justifies it.

clue.text: Economic growth?

parts.note: the phrase sounds like a rising GDP but means a plant connected with careful spending

explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful economy with money, and it is also a coastal plant, the sea pink.

clue.text: A woodman at play?

parts.note: a woodman here is a woodwind player, one who plays a double-reed instrument

explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, a woodwind instrument, so is a musician from the wind section.

clue.text: They serve people in queues

explanation.surface: Staff who bring food and those standing in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant staff bring plates to tables, and those standing in line are biding their time until called.

clue.text: How prices are displayed by pub laws

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
a code is a body of laws

explanation.surface: Drink prices at a pub are set by licensing rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop goods carry striped machine-readable labels that a scanner reads to give the price.

clue.text: Fire and water

explanation.surface: Flames and a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn is to be on fire, and in Scotland a burn is a small stream or brook.

clue.text: Realise it's a trick

explanation.surface: Understanding that one has been duped.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to sell it for money, and a sell is a hoax or swindle.

clue.text: Key leather treatment is delicate

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: treatment suggests working the leather over, so its letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A special leather finish is described as fine and dainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like the leather's quality but gives a musical note; 'treatment' is the anagram signal, and 'is' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means light and airy, unworldly in its fineness.

clue.text: Don't mention it, never

explanation.surface: A polite reply to thanks, and a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock reply when thanked, and it also emphatically means in no way whatsoever.

clue.text: Youth leader scoffs at a poet

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of youth

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffs means eats

explanation.surface: A youth group's head mocks a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffs' looks like mocking but means eating greedily; 'at a' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.
